title: Creative director's score of the Gate 3 board, first score (run 3)
author: Creative director (oa-creative-director), subagent of the main session
basis: work/handoffs/phase-3/20261120_Gate-3-Board-Brief.md, my row, "What the board holds" and "Limits"; Master Brief section 6 rubric; the board as the builder's run 3 left it (22:57 to 22:59 UTC, on version 14; 140,067 bytes; SHA-256 9ed7f6f790be0665…; 48 pictures), frozen with its pictures in scratchpad/c09/creative-director/frozen/ at 23:01 UTC and unchanged at 23:13; the Gate 3 report draft; the builder's notes; my apply pass rescore and its list "What the Gate 3 board must show from this pass". No browser opened: at 23:05 UTC the main session asked for the machine while the quick check with photographs runs, so every view is read from files. Panel 5's slot for this score and panel 7's two check slots wait, as the brief sets.
threshold: 4 on every criterion; the board ships when every score is 4 or more and it has no Must fix

items.name: The Gate 3 board as built (run 3, 22:59 UTC, on version 14)

reasons.craft: Each pair crops to its change at true size, and the page stands 47,753 px at 1440 and 66,047 at 390. The quoted report words set 75 straight apostrophes and six straight quotes beside 181 curled ones (G3-S1). Item 4 asks approval for two colors and shows no swatch (G3-S2). Two text pairs cut a line through its middle or sit flush on the text (G3-S12).
reasons.clarity: Answer-first items, a numbered list and the reply line let Dustin say what each item asks. Item 3 prints "D03 and D04" bare (G3-S3), panel 3 reprints board 3's closed alternative replies as if they were open (G3-S4), and panel 2 carries studio words (G3-S10).
reasons.brand_fidelity: The chrome uses eight token colors with no Pillar Red or Prussian, and with the name covered the page reads as Oath & Action by Newsprint, Inter Tight and the status chips. Two recommendations fall short of the settled list: item 7's scope leaves out DR-204 and DR-36 (G3-M4), and item 6's change to Rule 05.5 leaves two chapter 05 rules applying the keyline the atlas target dropped (G3-M3). The header still sets the name in live type, as boards 2 and 3 did.
reasons.usefulness: Dustin can answer all eleven in about six minutes, and every link resolves: 21 on the page, 23 to version 14's rules. Item 6 asks him to approve words he cannot see (G3-M3).
reasons.evidence_honesty: Two projections for one page (G3-M1). Item 5's reason claims more than the check does (G3-M2). Item 6 says each change "makes the guide say one thing in one way", which change (c) does not achieve alone (G3-M3). Panel 6 rates chapter 14 at 76.7 percent of a figure set for chapter 14 with the kit (G3-S6), and panel 7's chapter 14 check ran an hour before version 14 was built (G3-S8).
reasons.accessibility: By the builder's run the wrapped copy passes the board check at 1440, 390 and 360 px: no type under 13 px, no low contrast, no sideways scroll, 40 focus stops with rings. All 48 pictures carry their size, lazy loading and an alt that says what the picture shows, and the 12 tables are live text in labeled, focusable scroll regions. The three luma alts name the conversion and leave out what it shows (G3-S5).

items.to_ready: Fix G3-M1 to G3-M4: words in the report's sections 9 and 10, one figure the builder already reads, and the editor's words for Rule 05.5 with Rules 05.3 and 05.7. Brand fidelity and evidence honesty reach 4 when those land. The Shoulds are small and block nothing.

G3-M1.title: Two projections for one page.
G3-M1.where: Panel 6, first table, the two rows "The page as projected with every chapter built" (15,180,545; 94.9 and 97.9 percent); panel 2, "Page weight", last paragraph ("puts the page about 150,545 bytes past the 15.5 MB line").
G3-M1.what: Panel 6 reads the build report's projection, which counts each of Phase 4's seven chapters at 362,857 bytes, 2,539,999 in all. Panel 2's allocations total 3,010,000 and put the page at 15,650,545 bytes. Panel 6 shows the page under the warning line and panel 2 shows it past.
G3-M1.fix: Label panel 6's rows "as the build projects it today, with each Phase 4 chapter at 362,857 bytes", and add a row "with panel 2's allocations: 15,650,545 bytes, 97.8 percent of 16 MB and 101.0 percent of the 15.5 MB line", both read from the build report and panel 2's figures.

G3-M2.title: Item 5 promises more than the check does.
G3-M2.where: Panel 1, item 5's recommendation and its line under "The 11 items".
G3-M2.what: "so a later chart cannot run a line through its own label". The check is the kit's edge guard, which fails a band's edge drawn through a value label that a form marks for clearance (20261120_Label-Clearance-List.json, "what_this_is"; the engineer's A4 row). Panel 4's first line says so. A series line, an axis, a leader or another label crossing a word lies outside it, so "As proposed" approves a narrower guard than the sentence describes.
G3-M2.fix: "Switch it on for every chart, so no band's edge, such as a fan chart's range, can run through a value label." Add under "What it covers": "It tests band edges only; a line, axis or label crossing a word stays for the maker and the reviewer to catch."

G3-M3.title: Item 6 asks for changes to approved rules without their words, and change (c) leaves two rules saying the opposite.
G3-M3.what: Changes (a) and (b) have exact words in the register ("takes the text’s ink at any size", "The text’s ink, with the label (Rule 05.1)", "except a chip’s ID (Rule 18.24)"); the board prints a summary of each. Change (c) has no drafted words. Rule 05.3's reason says a working red mark on Newsprint "takes a keyline … (Rule 05.5)", and its rule names "where a reform acts" as a working red job. Rule 05.7, whose title covers charts and the atlas, gives the named point "a Charcoal keyline, as in Rule 05.5". With 05.5 alone changed, chapter 05 still says two things about the atlas target.
G3-M3.fix: Print each change as today's words beside the proposed words. The editor drafts (c)'s sentence for Rule 05.5 and the matching words for Rule 05.3's reason; for Rule 05.7, the same exception, or one line on why a chart's named point keeps its keyline. Name all three rules in (c).
G3-M3.owner: Editor (words), through the main session (report section 10 and the register row); builder rebuilds.

G3-M4.title: Item 7's scope leaves out two settled answers.
G3-M4.where: Panel 2, "What Phase 4 produces", rows 20 and 21, and "The checks Phase 4 runs"; panel 1, item 7.
G3-M4.what: DR-204 gives every screen product one dark mode, drawn from Night Edition on Charcoal, following the reader's device setting, with a visible switch that remembers the choice. Chapters 20 and 21 name no dark mode or switch, and no check captures one. Chapter 21 is "drawn from Concepts 03, 09, 10 and 11", the Master Brief's words from before DR-36, and the row never names the atlas visual system Dustin settled (DR-36, moved to Newsprint by DR-121) or its finishing list. Under gate rule 3, work outside an approved proposal waits for the next gate, so both need to sit in the words he approves.
G3-M4.fix: Chapter 20's row adds "every page on Newsprint and in the dark mode, with its switch". Chapter 21's row reads "in the atlas visual system you settled, on Newsprint, finished by its list, with views drawn from Concepts 03 Field Manual, 09 The Circuit, 10 Who Can Act and 11 Register". The checks add "Each web and atlas page in its dark mode at 1440 and 390 px, with the switch reached by keyboard and remembered". The reference line adds DR-36, DR-121 and DR-204.

G3-S1.title: Curl the quoted words
G3-S1.what_and_fix: Panels 1, 2, 5 and 7 quote the report with 75 straight apostrophes and six straight double quotes, beside 181 curled ones; item 6 sets "Charcoal" in straight quotes. Master Brief section 6 asks for correct quotation marks and apostrophes. Curl them at build, or in the report.

G3-S2.title: Show item 4's colors
G3-S2.what_and_fix: Two swatches on Charcoal at true size, #828A9D and #505C7D with their ratios, and plain words first ("two lighter Prussians for the diverging scale on Charcoal"); the token names can sit in small type.
G3-S2.owner: builder; main session for the words

G3-S3.title: Name item 3's two domains
G3-S3.what_and_fix: "D03 and D04's reform counts" prints bare codes (H11). Write "the reform counts of two atlas domains, Money, lobbying and influence, and Congress, agencies and public services".

G3-S4.what_and_fix: "What you approved" for replies 7, 11 and 18 still ends "To update both, reply “Chapter 02 too”", "For a keyline on every red target, reply “Keyline everywhere”" and "For a stated search instead, reply “Run the search”". At Gate 3 they read as replies open now. Drop them, or set each as "Board 3's other choice, not taken".

G3-S5.what_and_fix: Under "The same three red targets in luma", add: "In gray, each chosen pill's red ring reads lighter than a plain pill's black edge, so the target is the faintest mark, and the words beside each plate carry it." Give each luma alt that fact.

G3-S6.what_and_fix: It rates chapter 14 without the kit at 76.7 percent of 2,803,941, the figure set for chapter 14 with the kit, which the first table rates at 101.9 percent. Print "Chapter 14 without the kit; with it, 101.9 percent (above)", or drop the row.

G3-S8.what_and_fix: It is the engineer's run of 21:13 to 21:15 UTC, an hour before version 14 was built at 22:21. Read the main session's closing run on the final files, or say the run predates version 14.

G3-S9.title: P4-3 asks for a permission the brief already gives

Say so, then ask what is open: whether Canva's or Figma's terms suit the rights ledger, and whether the default stays narrower than the brief.

G3-S11.title: Reply 6's captions
G3-S11.what_and_fix: They read "The kit’s export S14 exported for a 1440 px page". Write "S14 as the kit exports it alone, for a 1440 px page, on Newsprint", and the same for Charcoal.

phase_4_view.verdict: Approve it with additions. The engine is right: one application kit on the chart kit's model, drawn at build time, exports beside the guide, a dimension script and safe-area overlays, and the channel table holds DR-292's eight channels with every application Master Brief section 18 lists. As written it would produce applications at the right sizes in the right places; four gaps stand between that and finished work at the bar.
scope: Web (20): add the home page and one Act page at the four widths, and DR-204's dark mode with its switch (G3-M4).
Atlas (21): name DR-36's system and its finishing list (G3-M4).

Substack and email (22): one chart inside a post as a still image with alt and source line (DR-49, DR-59); the working email with a dark-mode pass, a plain-text part, alt on every image and HTML small enough that Gmail shows it whole (about 102 KB, for the research lead to confirm).

Social (23): each profile as a reader meets it, avatar over banner at desktop and phone width; S95's 1080 x 1920 frame held by DR-268; DR-116's avatar and DR-211's 96 px sign-off; the web address held as DR-55 set.

Reports and print (24, 25): the sizes Master Brief section 18 asks for (US Letter with bleed and margins, 24 x 36 in poster, 11 x 17 in table sign), the print lockup of DR-210, and DR-102 for an event piece with a host.

Photography (16): placeholders cannot teach a selection, crop or caption rule; a fifth question could let chapter 16 teach on two or three public-domain federal photographs, as chapter 01 does (DR-238), each with a rights row, while Q-04 stays open.
phase_4_view.allocations: The arithmetic holds: 3,359,455 bytes of room, 3,010,000 allocated (89.6 percent), 349,455 in reserve. The method sizes each chapter by its count of rules, and the two chapters with the most drawing get the thinnest margins: chapter 23 sits 0.4 percent above its own estimate (20 rules at 32,856) and chapter 20 2.8 percent (10 at 48,651); chapter 23's analog draws little and chapter 20's holds no dark mode. In chat 10, measure the kit's bytes for a social post, a web page at four widths with its dark mode and a report page, re-size the seven, and show it on Phase 4 board 1. Chapter 27's 200,000 must index every export.

Board 1's decisions should add the atlas's views with its system test, and chapter 16's rules.

distinctiveness_test.view: The cover and chrome, read from the page's style and the check's runs (no browser)
distinctiveness_test.verdict: A Newsprint ground, Inter Tight display at 800, one Charcoal rule, the status chips, and no red mark in the chrome (the check counts none).
They carry the brand by themselves: the red target, the evidence chips and the lockmark at the end of S14's source line.

risks_for_dustin: On paper Phase 4 starts past the 15.5 MB warning line with 349,455 bytes, about 2 percent of the page, in reserve; every Phase 4 build will warn until the line moves, which is his word under DR-271.
The label check, switched on for every chart, guards band edges only (G3-M2).
The atlas target is the faintest mark in gray print and one-ink copies; the words carry it, and "Keyline everywhere" stays his named alternative.
The chart kit's exports run their ink to the artboard's edge; a chart posted alone in Phase 4 needs a margin.
for_the_register: The kit's exports have no margin: on the data lead's S14 build at 2x the lockmark's lever sits 2 px from the right and bottom edges of the 1440 PNG (x 1428 to 1437 of 1440, y 1258 to 1267 of 1270) and the source line's ink starts at x 1. Rule 08.2 sets a sign-off inside the margin. Propose clear space of at least the lockmark's own 16 px round every export, for the application kit's first build or the finishing pass. My apply pass rescore read these exports and missed the edge; the kit's craft stays at 4 and this row decides whether it holds.
Version 14's build report counts each Phase 4 chapter at 362,857 bytes; once Dustin answers item 7, the build takes panel 2's allocations so its projection and warning read true.
